note: 256 binary files v1/XX.json.bin (about 185 MB), transcode_json.py converts. Generated by Mesen: A X Y S P PC MPR[8], sparse RAM on a flat 2 MB physical space, per-cycle [address21, data, 'r-d' pins]. Block moves truncated at 500 cycles/500 RAM pairs. Emulator-derived; the author says it is 'only as good as Mesen'.

The CMOS sets (wdc65c02, rockwell65c02, synertek65c02: 256 files x 10,000 cases, per-cycle [address, value, read/write]) are pinned by revision but only their READMEs are checked out in Phase 0; widen the sparse list to /wdc65c02/ or /rockwell65c02/ for rung 1b. Emulator-derived.
The source of tag mame0285, the installed /usr/games/mame. h6280.cpp/.h (the core, 7.16/1.79 MHz divider, MMU, timer, IRQ), pce.cpp (the driver). Emulator-derived.
Mesen2's PCE core. Generated SingleStepTests huc6280; its authors claim the most accurate HuC6280 emulation (unverified here). Emulator-derived.

Mednafen's accurate PCE core (huc6280.cpp), as libretro's Beetle PCE. Covell's page says Mednafen's CPU timing matches hardware. Emulator-derived. Mednafen proper can be built from its source tarball if a second referee is wanted; see docs/validation.md.
Mednafen's fast PCE core (instruction-level cycle counts). Emulator-derived; a second implementation of the same table.
ares HuC6280 component + PCE CPU wrapper (timer, IRQ, I/O). Emulator-derived.
Geargrafx HuC6280 (timing header, block transfers, speed change). Emulator-derived.

srg320's HuC6280 in VHDL (microcoded, hand-written: not die-traced), and the authors' logic-analyser screenshots of opcode timing at 42.95 MHz in docs/logs. The VHDL is an FPGA re-implementation, emulator tier; the screenshots are images of captures of a real console.
The HuC/PCEAS assembler: its instruction tables are a community encoding reference for the opcode map, bytes and addressing modes. Research.
